info.description: Backend API for Brndr. Routes accept and return application/x-protobuf payloads unless otherwise noted.
info.title: Brndr API

post.description: Records (/api/block) or lifts (/api/unblock) the caller's block of the target. A block withdraws BOTH likes and leaves the pair unmatched, but the thread stays in the hub on both sides — readable, category UNMATCHED_VISIBLE, flagged while the block stands (person.blocked); an unblock only drops the flag, and only a mutual re-like restores the match. Likes and messages between the pair are refused while severed. Both block and unblock are idempotent.
Returns the ids of the people the caller has blocked (who blocked the caller is never exposed).
Stores a batch of browsing elements (accounts the user saw, with timestamps) for the authenticated user. Uploads are idempotent and safe to retry.

get.description: Returns the active community-board posts ("Vývěska") — not yet expired, newest first. Blocked authors' posts are NOT filtered: the client drops them with its own block list ("flags, not filters").

post.description: Publishes a board post as the authenticated user. The server normalizes the draft: title/desc trimmed and capped (80/400 chars), days clamped to 1-30, looking chips only on the extended template (trimmed, capped, at most 6). Returns the stored post (id, author, timestamps).
Deletes one of the caller's own board posts (author check: 403 for anybody else's post, 404 when the post does not exist).

Issues a one-time code to a student email (6 digits, 10 min TTL). At most one send per address per minute; a resend replaces any previous code. Delivery needs BRNDR_SMTP_PASS on the server — otherwise the code is logged, not sent (dev mode).

Checks the submitted one-time code for the address. 204 on match (the address is marked verified — and any UNAUTH account with that email is ACTIVATED: locked accounts become usable), 400 when no code was requested or the code is wrong/expired, 429 after too many wrong attempts (request a new code).

400.description: No code / wrong or expired code

post.description: Returns the authenticated user's connections with server-computed categories (chats/matches/likes/requests). peer_id set scopes the answer to that one entry — the websocket Interaction_Changed hint names the peer to re-fetch this way.

get.description: Returns any user's published E2EE public key (32 B raw X25519) — peers seal messages to it, the owner compares it against the locally derived key for drift detection. Empty public_key = the user has not published one (send plaintext). Authenticated: no anonymous bulk scrape of key material; any authenticated user may fetch any user's key — public keys are public by design.
get.summary: Fetch a user's E2EE public key

post.description: Returns any user's published E2EE public key (32 B raw X25519) — peers seal messages to it, the owner compares it against the locally derived key for drift detection. Empty public_key = the user has not published one (send plaintext). Authenticated: no anonymous bulk scrape of key material; any authenticated user may fetch any user's key — public keys are public by design.
post.summary: Fetch a user's E2EE public key

post.description: Publishes the caller's E2EE public key — write-once: it only succeeds while no key is published (409 otherwise), so a stolen token cannot swap a key out from under existing conversations. Publishing again after a deliberate /api/key/reset works. Exactly 32 bytes (raw X25519).

409.description: A key is already published (reset first)

post.description: Clears the caller's published public key AND wrapped-key blob in one transaction — the explicit recovery for a deleted passkey, a device reset or a confirmed drift warning. Afterwards /api/key/publish succeeds again and the client enrolls a fresh identity. Messages encrypted to the previous key become irrecoverable (inherent to the design). The account password is required: a bare stolen token must not be able to destroy message readability (the same friction as /api/delete).

get.description: Returns the caller's own password-wrapped private key (the fallback identity blob: public key, wrapped private key, PBKDF2 salt and iteration count — opaque to the server, which never parses it). Self only: the authenticated user is the owner, there is no user_id on the wire. Empty response = no fallback identity stored. The blob is offline-attackable, so fetches are rate-limited (429 + Retry-After) and logged.

429.description: Too many fetches; Retry-After header set

post.description: Returns the caller's own password-wrapped private key (the fallback identity blob: public key, wrapped private key, PBKDF2 salt and iteration count — opaque to the server, which never parses it). Self only: the authenticated user is the owner, there is no user_id on the wire. Empty response = no fallback identity stored. The blob is offline-attackable, so fetches are rate-limited (429 + Retry-After) and logged.

429.description: Too many fetches; Retry-After header set

post.description: Stores (or replaces — the normal "wipe local state, re-wrap" flow) the caller's password-wrapped private key blob. The server keeps it opaque; only the shape is validated: public_key exactly 32 B, wrapped_private_key 1-256 B, kdf_salt 1-32 B, kdf_iterations >= 100000. The client saves this BEFORE publishing the public key: a wrapped key without a published key is a harmless half-state its owner resolves by re-creating the identity.

Records a like (/api/like) or removes it (/api/unlike) for the target user. Users cannot like themselves. Unlike after a match is a no-op (matches are permanent). The resulting hub state is read from /api/interactions.

Returns the ids of the people the caller currently likes (their outgoing likes; who liked the caller lives in the hub's LIKES/REQUESTS entries). Pre-match and matched alike; a pre-match unlike, a block or an unmatch withdraws the like, unlike after a match is a no-op. A first/unmatched message attaches the sender's like.

get.description: Returns the authenticated user's own view: the shared identity, both kind-profiles, and the account facts only the owner may read (username, email, city). The public /profile lookup cannot return these — they live on Me_Return, not Person_Profile.

post.description: Toggles the authenticated user's emoji reaction on a message (same emoji twice = remove). Only the sender or a recipient of the message may react; a blocked-pair thread is refused (400). The updated reaction state is read back via the message endpoints.

404.description: Message not found for this user

post.description: Issues a one-time code to the account's email (6 digits, 10 min TTL). At most one send per address per minute; a resend replaces any previous code. Always 204 — even for an address with no account, so the endpoint cannot be used to enumerate registered emails. Only ACTIVE accounts get a code (stored and mailed); a syntactically invalid address is 400. Delivery needs BRNDR_SMTP_PASS on the server — otherwise the code is logged, not sent (dev mode).

Checks the submitted one-time code and, on match, installs the new bcrypt password in the same call. The account's E2EE identity is deleted (the old password wrapped the private key — old messages become unreadable; the user re-enrolls on next use) and the live refresh token is revoked. 400 when no code was requested or the code is wrong/expired or the new password is empty, 429 after too many wrong attempts (request a new code). The reset code is single-use.
post.summary: Verify a reset code and set the new password

400.description: No code / wrong or expired code / bad new password

post.description: Uploads an image (max 2 MB): webp inputs (the client's compressed format) are stored verbatim, other image formats are converted to webp, non-images are refused. Returns the stored image url.

Stores a client-side-encrypted photo as an opaque blob: no decode, no re-encode, no format sniffing — the raw bytes are hashed (sha256 of the CIPHERTEXT, never the plaintext: no confirmation oracle), written to public/encrypted/<hash>.bin (identical bytes dedup to the same file) and served back at /uploads/encrypted/<hash>.bin as application/octet-stream with nosniff. The URL and the decryption key travel inside the sealed message body, never here. Max 1.5 MB; 30 uploads per hour per user.

429.description: Upload rate limit; Retry-After header set

post.description: Persists editable profile fields. Name, pohlavi, faculty and birth (year+month, stored on the last day of the month) are shared across profile kinds; bio, height, sex, orientation, relationship, interests and photos are written only to the request's `kind` profile (created on first write).

get.description: Returns all messages for the authenticated user.

post.description: Stores an encrypted message for the recipients. An optional reply_to references a prior message of the same thread (visible to the sender); an invisible reply target is rejected. A first/unmatched send attaches the sender's like (so opening on someone who already liked you matches instantly).

400.description: Bad request (bad/foreign reply target, duplicate recipient)

get.description: Returns user suggestions matching the search filters.

post.description: Records (/api/block) or lifts (/api/unblock) the caller's block of the target. A block withdraws BOTH likes and leaves the pair unmatched, but the thread stays in the hub on both sides — readable, category UNMATCHED_VISIBLE, flagged while the block stands (person.blocked); an unblock only drops the flag, and only a mutual re-like restores the match. Likes and messages between the pair are refused while severed. Both block and unblock are idempotent.

Records a like (/api/like) or removes it (/api/unlike) for the target user. Users cannot like themselves. Unlike after a match is a no-op (matches are permanent). The resulting hub state is read from /api/interactions.

Tombstones the pair's relation on both sides: the thread leaves both hubs, likes are withdrawn, the message history is kept. A later like or message from either side revives the thread; a mutual re-like restores the match. Idempotent.

Irreversibly deletes the authenticated user's account: profiles, relations, sent messages, blocks, reports, browsing telemetry and community posts all cascade away at the database level; the login token and every live websocket connection are torn down. The account password is required — a stolen token alone cannot destroy an account. Peers lose the pair's hub entry and the user's sent messages, but keep their own side of every thread. Idempotent: an already-deleted account still returns 204 with its session revoked.

401.description: Unauthorized (bad token, or the account no longer exists)

post.description: Sets the caller's ghost flag for one kind. discoverable=false removes the user from that kind's discovery surfaces (the kind feeds, suggestions — and, once every presented kind is hidden, the /api/profile search) and refuses their initiations there (likes in that kind; first-contact messages while fully hidden). Existing connections are unaffected. The current state is read from /api/me (Me_Return.discoverable_*). Idempotent; setting discoverable=true un-hides.

get.description: Returns profiles for the swipe feed (ordered list; a cursor can come later). Hidden users are excluded: a user hidden in the feed's kind (or, for the bare feed, in every kind they present) cannot be found here; existing connections are unaffected (the interaction hub keeps them). Every person carries both profiles; ?kind=dating|friendship narrows the feed to users presenting that mode.

parameters.description: Only users presenting this kind's profile
parameters.name: kind

post.description: Exchanges username + password (bcrypt, set at /register) for the account id and a refresh token — the only way to obtain one. An UNAUTH account (registered, email not yet verified) is refused with 403; without a token no private endpoint (or websocket) is reachable.

Revokes the authenticated user's login token: the token (and every live websocket connection of the user) stops working immediately — re-login is the only way back. The client discards its copy; the server-side revocation is what makes logout real.

get.description: Returns every user matching the query (id, name, email), each with the shared identity and both profiles. Private since 2026-09-05 (SECURITY_AUDIT P0: the public lookup was a bulk-scraping hole — the email/name search in particular). Blocked pairs are flagged (person.blocked), never filtered — "flags, not filters". Fully-hidden users (every presented kind hidden, 2026-09-05) are not findable here; partially hidden ones are (they exist in their discoverable kinds) — existing connections reach them through the hub.

parameters.description: Profile query payload (at least one of id/name/email)
parameters.name: body

post.description: Creates an account. The email must be a student address (vut.cz domain only — not vutbr.cz, per the 2026-09-05 decision). An UNVERIFIED email still creates the account, but it stays locked — no login token (/api/login refuses it) until the email is verified through /api/email/verify-code. Fails if the username is already taken.

get.description: Upgrades the connection to a WebSocket. First message must be a valid Auth_Read protobuf.
Returns the global list of zajmy (interests).

element.description:
Types that are valid to be assigned to Element:

	*Browsing_Element_Account

discoverable.description: True = visible and findable (the default); false = hidden in that kind.

x-enum-comments.Interaction_Category_INTERACTION_LOCKED: I opened, no mutual like: locked until they like back
x-enum-comments.Interaction_Category_INTERACTION_UNMATCH: match removed on purpose; tombstone, hidden from the hub

x-enum-descriptions: I opened, no mutual like: locked until they like back
match removed on purpose; tombstone, hidden from the hub

last_message.description:
The pair's latest message, encrypted for the fetching user; absent
when the thread has no messages (2026-09-03).

updated_at.description: Last hub activity (message or state change), epoch ms — row ordering.

peer_id.description:
0 = the whole hub; otherwise exactly this peer's entry from the
viewer's perspective (absent when hidden from the viewer).

public_key.description: 32 B raw X25519; EMPTY = the user has no published key.

kdf_salt.description: 16 B PBKDF2 salt (CLIENT-side KDF — unrelated to users.salt).

zajmy.description: Interest ids into the /zajmy catalog (string ids, 2026-09-03).

matched.description:
True when this like formed a mutual match — or, on unlike, when the
pair is matched (unlike after a match is a no-op: matches are
permanent). The resulting hub state is read from /api/interactions (and,
later, delivered as a websocket Interaction_Updated event).

city.description: Account-level fact, shared across both kind profiles.

discoverable_dating.description:
Per-kind discoverability ("ghost mode", 2026-09-05): false while the
user is hidden in that kind (set through /api/discovery). True when the
kind has no profile at all (the default — nothing to hide).

username.description: Login name (users.jmeno); the display name is Person_Profile.name.

id.description:
Stable storage id, assigned by the server: reactions and replies
reference it (added 2026-09-03).

peer_id.description:
The other party from the fetching user's perspective: the sender for
received messages, the (other) recipient for own sent messages.

reactions.description: Reactions on this message, from the fetching user's perspective.

reply_to.description: Storage id of the message this one replies to; 0 = not a reply.

sender_id.description:
Routing metadata for thread bucketing (added 2026-08-04, G4): without a
sender id the client cannot tell own bubbles from theirs; without the
peer id it cannot group messages per conversation when only the
fetching user's key is enclosed.

from_me.description: True when the fetching user placed this reaction.

age.description: Exact birthday-aware age derived from users.birth_date (migration 00007).

blocked.description:
True when a block stands between the viewer and this person, in EITHER
direction (2026-09-04 "flags, not filters" contract): the server never
hides blocked people from payloads — it labels them, and the client
renders the blocked state (actions disabled; the server refuses them
anyway, migration 00004 triggers). The blocker's own client already
knows the direction from /api/blocked.

faculty.description:
VUT faculty key ('FIT', 'FaVU', …; 2026-09-05) from the shared
vocabulary (vocab/fakulty.go). Public — it renders on profile cards.
Empty = not set („už nestuduji“).

name.description: Shared identity (account-level, identical for both kinds).

kind.description: Which profile the uploaded photo belongs to (2026-09-02).

birth_year.description:
Account-level birth (2026-09-05): the user picks year+month only, the
day is unknown by design. The server stores users.birth_date on the
LAST day of that month ("assume it is the last day of the month"),
so the birthday-aware exact_age turns the age on the month's last
day — the same convention the frontend's ageFromBirth uses.
Zero = keep (never cleared; same as the other identity fields).

city.description: Account-level, shared across kinds (2026-09-03). Empty = keep.

faculty.description:
Account-level VUT faculty key ('FIT', 'FaVU', …; 2026-09-05), shared
across kinds. Empty = keep (same as city). Validated against the
shared vocabulary (vocab/fakulty.go — the same keys the frontend's
FACULTIES uses); there is deliberately no CHECK constraint, so adding
a faculty is a vocab change, not a migration.

zajmy.description: Interest ids into the /zajmy catalog (string ids, 2026-09-03).

id.description:
String id from the moderated vocabulary (2026-09-03); the frontend's
interest ids are this id.
